about.title: Personal Injury Help in Long Beach, California
about.longDescription: As home to one of the nation's busiest ports, Long Beach mixes heavy truck traffic with dense neighborhoods and beachfront tourism. Public records show more than 2,100 injury collisions in the city in 2025, leaving over 3,100 people hurt, with reported crashes tending to peak on Friday evenings. Corridors like Atlantic Avenue, Long Beach Boulevard, Pacific Coast Highway and the I-405 (San Diego Freeway) carry a constant flow of cars, big rigs, cyclists and pedestrians. Whether you were injured in a wreck, in a fall at a business, in a workplace or port-area incident, or by a defective product, California law gives you rights and a limited time to use them. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Long Beach with an independent personal injury attorney who understands how Los Angeles County claims and courts work. We are not a law firm; we simply match you with counsel. There is never a fee unless your case recovers compensation.

whyChoose.title: What Long Beach injury victims should know

items.title: Usually a 2-year deadline
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file. Around a busy port, dashcam and traffic-camera footage can vanish within days, so acting early protects your claim.

items.title: Partial fault still recovers
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so you can recover even if you were partly to blame; your compensation is reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: Truck cases can involve many parties
items.desc: A crash with a commercial truck may involve the driver, the carrier and others. An attorney can identify every responsible party and insurer.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: Most California injury cases place no limit on non-economic damages, so the human toll of your injury can be part of your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Long Beach?
items.answer: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years. Claims against a public entity — a city vehicle or hazardous public road — can carry a deadline as short as six months, so speak with an attorney quickly.

items.question: What if the accident was partly my fault?
items.answer: You can still recover. California uses pure comparative fault, so your award is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated.

items.question: A truck was involved — is my case different?
items.answer: Often yes. Commercial-truck claims can involve multiple insurers and federal safety rules, and evidence like driver logs must be preserved quickly. An attorney can act to secure it.

items.question: What does a case review cost?
items.answer: Nothing. The review is free and attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no attorney fee unless they recover compensation for you.

items.question: Where do injury crashes cluster in Long Beach?
items.answer: Reported-collision records for recent years point to Atlantic Avenue, Long Beach Boulevard, Pacific Coast Highway and the I-405, with crashes peaking on Friday evenings. These are public-record counts, not a verdict about any road.
